evidence: app/package.json:7 — entire app runs on @gracile/gracile 0.11.0, released ~6 months ago; project docs self-label the framework 'alpha state' (gracile.js.org/docs)
app/vite.config.ts:4-6 — only documented plugin option used (output: 'server'); no experimental flags anywhere in app/
app/src/routes/index.ts:1 — every page uses defineRoute/handler/document, the framework's core documented API surface
app/src/routes/index.client.ts:16 — no CSR router or hydration API; vanilla window.location.assign for filter navigation
app/package.json:8-10 — lit 3.3.3, express ^5.3.0, vite ^8.3.5: all stable releases (Vite 8 stable since 2026-03-12)
reach.rationale: The whole app sits on a young, self-described-alpha framework in central places (0.11.0, ~6 months old) because the spec mandates it, but every framework API touched is the documented core of the current stable release — no experimental flags, previews or canary features are reached for, and the riskier parts of the framework (hydration, custom elements, CSR, add-ons) are deliberately avoided.

evidence: app/src/routes/index.ts:35 — undocumented 'gracile-static' hostname sentinel used to detect Gracile's build-time handler stub
app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].ts:104 — same sentinel duplicated rather than wrapped in one helper
app/src/routes/abilities/[name].ts:19, app/src/routes/types/[name].ts:24, app/src/routes/moves/[name].ts:28 — sentinel repeated in 5 route files total
app/src/routes/types/index.ts:8-11 — this data-fetching handler lacks the sentinel guard, unlike its siblings, so containment is inconsistent
app/server.js:2-10 — node adapter and client build path are cleanly confined to the server entrypoint, matching the official engine JSDoc example
containment.rationale: Framework usage is necessarily app-wide, but the single undocumented internal reliance (the 'gracile-static' build sentinel) is copy-pasted across five route files instead of being isolated in one shared guard, and one route (types/index.ts) omits it entirely — partly contained at best.

evidence: app/package.json:7 — spec mandates Gracile with Lit; pinning the exact current stable release (0.11.0) is the low-risk choice for an alpha framework
app/src/routes/index.ts:35-49 — sentinel guard exists to satisfy SPEC.md's rule against build-time API fetching; no documented API distinguishes Gracile's build-time stub handler call

app/src/routes/index.client.ts:1-18, app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].client.ts:1-16 — choosing plain DOM scripts over the framework's newer client-router/hydration layers avoids APIs the docs describe as not yet built-in or in flux
app/src/document.ts:1 — server-html html is the documented document API; no experimental add-ons imported anywhere (grep of app/src shows none)
justification.rationale: Each use buys something a stable alternative couldn't: the mandated framework, its documented core APIs, and the sentinel guard needed to keep data fetching off the build path. One point off because the guard leans on an undocumented internal rather than a supported mechanism.

findings.issue: Handlers rely on the undocumented 'gracile-static' URL-hostname sentinel to detect Gracile's build-time stub handler invocation (confirmed in @gracile/engine src/routes/render.ts but absent from public docs), and the same string is duplicated in pokemon/[name].ts:104, abilities/[name].ts:19, types/[name].ts:24 and moves/[name].ts:28
findings.suggestion: Extract the check into one shared helper (e.g. lib/build-stub.ts exporting isBuildStub(url)) with a comment citing the engine source, so a framework change only needs fixing in one place

findings.issue: Unlike the other four data routes, this handler has no sentinel guard, so Gracile calls it with the build-time stub URL and it fetches /type/ from the API during npm run build
findings.suggestion: Apply the same build-stub guard (or the shared helper) for consistency and to guarantee no build-time network dependency on the API server

findings.issue: The whole app rests on @gracile/gracile 0.11.0, a pre-1.0 framework whose own documentation cautions it is in an alpha state, so breaking changes across minor versions are likely
findings.suggestion: Keep the exact version pin, record it as a known platform risk in the README, and budget for migration work when bumping

findings.issue: vite ^8.3.5 is only recently-stable (8.0 released 2026-03-12, first release on the new Rolldown bundler), so build tooling is on the newest major line
findings.suggestion: Acceptable; just verify builds when Vite 8.x minors land, since the app depends on Gracile's Vite plugin interacting correctly with it

summary: The app reaches for zero experimental flags, previews or canary APIs: it uses only the documented core surface of Gracile's current stable release (0.11.0, itself ~6 months old and self-labeled alpha by its own docs), and deliberately avoids the framework's less-settled layers in favor of vanilla DOM scripts. The one risky spot is reliance on the undocumented 'gracile-static' build sentinel, duplicated across five route files and inconsistently applied (types/index.ts lacks it). Overall risk is moderate and driven mostly by the mandated framework's alpha status, not by the app's API choices.
